pages.lesson:
LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: VISUALS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing 3.6 Guided Writing: Sentences (2 sessions) • Descriptive words • Simple 
Topic 3.8: Guided Writing: Visuals

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing: Visuals. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do weather patterns affect our daily life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. appreciate summary writing as a key skill in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING: VISUALS
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Writing: Visuals helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED WRITING: VISUALS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Appreciate summary writing as a key skill in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate summary writing as a key skill in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate summary writing as a key skill in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Visuals”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate summary writing as a key skill in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Writing: Visuals is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Visuals”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate summary writing as a key skill in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Writing: Visuals to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: appreciate summary writing as a key skill in communication.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Writing: Visuals from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Writing: Visuals: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Guided Writing: Visuals?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do weather patterns affect our daily life?
2. Why are pictures considered to be worth a thousand words?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Writing: Visuals means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: appreciate summary writing as a key skill in communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
